extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Popular Science Monthly — scientifically literate general public, practitioners and students in architecture, engineering, medicine, natural history, and related arts/sciences
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria used in short critical notices and reviews of books and works (architecture, sanitary guides, natural-history atlases, astronomy guides, medical treatises) intended for a scientifically literate magazine audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architecture should express ideas by structures
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the province of architecture to express ideas by structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a man builds a house doing nothing for show and everything for structural integrity so that it may serve his purpose, his house will be a monument to his purpose; architecture should make structure itself convey idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and technical principles are essential to proficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: In all other branches of knowledge, study and acquaintance with technical principles are considered essential to even a fair degree of proficiency. So it is with architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combat reliance on mere taste or common sense; technical training prevents the ill-adapted buildings that result from ignorance of principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on taste/common sense alone
rubrics_metrics.description: The evil effects of too great reliance on taste, and too little attention to training, are illustrated in the ill-adapted buildings that we meet everywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taste alone is not the quality that enables production or judgement of works of art; professional study and technical acquaintance are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish an organic relation between ornament and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: It is useless to seek for a clew to all this in the organism of the monument itself, or in the nature of the idea which has called it into existence, or to seek to establish an organic relation between the ornament and the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Looseness of definition of architecture that ignores organism and idea leads to false conceptions and illogical reasoning; ornament should arise from structure/idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conscientious execution and respect for the work
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to create a monument it is necessary that its author should be conscientious, and that he should respect the thing he is doing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not resort to mechanical expedients merely because they are economical if they detract from clear art expression; exercise self-denial and refrain from unmeaning display for show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty derives from clear expression of the idea in matter
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no beauty but that which results from a forcible, clear, and successful expression of the idea in matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty must depend on the amount of character in various features of the structure; superficial decoration without idea lacks true beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form must correspond with function (express acts performed within)
rubrics_metrics.description: The problem is mainly to give expression to the acts performed within its walls, which is done by giving the structure a form which will correspond with the groups performing those acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give parts such masses, modeling, carved and color decoration as will express precisely the degree of stability, dignity, and elegance corresponding with the import of the acts to be expressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Root out dilettanteism and false taste; pursue architecture seriously
rubrics_metrics.description: The dilettanteism of modern architecture must be rooted out before the art can revive; false taste has had its day, and style must be cast off, when nothing will be left but to pursue architecture pure and simple.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The road to architecture is long, tortuous, and thorny, requiring training and seriousness rather than an easy pursuit of fame through style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pictorial representation to describe sanitary defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictorial representation chosen as the most impressive way of describing faults of domestic sanitary arrangements to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seventy plates represent nearly as many important faults with accompanying letterpress explanations; illustrations designed to give the most forcible expression possible of the fact to be told.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations must be clear and distinct in meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations are designed to give the most forcible expression possible of the fact to be told, and are clear and distinct as to their meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals should communicate the sanitary fault unambiguously; some drawings can serve as practical hints (e.g., ventilation/exclusion of dust).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical directions and explanatory text for students
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the Zoological Atlas is to help the student in the explanation and dissection of the leading forms of animal life; the function of a book is to assist in practical study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow pedagogical principles emphasizing specimen examination; text should be practical, brief, and directly tied to dissection practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrations should highlight points to note with brief explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The illustrations, which are colored, represent the various points to be noted in the dissections, showing the details of anatomical structure and their relations, and are accompanied by suitable and brief explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plates must show external/internal characters, skeleton, nervous and sense organs, alimentary, circulatory, respiratory systems, etc., in a concise explanatory style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select specimens for convenience and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The six types of vertebral life are represented by a specimen selected with reference to its convenience of size for handling and the facility of procuring it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose species (e.g., skate, cod, salamander, tortoise, pigeon, rabbit) that are practical for student dissection and readily obtainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide plain practical guidance for amateur instrument users
rubrics_metrics.description: Celestial Objects for Common Telescopes: purpose is to furnish the possessors of ordinary telescopes with plain directions for their use, and a list of objects for their advantageous employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include descriptions of the instrument, care and use directions, and lists/maps of observable objects suited to ordinary refractors (3–5 in.) and small reflectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize observational guides by navigational/constellation scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: The chapter on double stars, clusters, and nebulae is arranged by constellations, under the head of which each object is specifically and separately located and described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply moon and planetary maps (e.g., moon sheet-map, Mars polar map) and specific locating information for practical observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present differences of authority impartially but give reasoned personal view
rubrics_metrics.description: The Verbalist follows a strictly alphabetical arrangement of words and topics in regard to which a wrong usage exists or authorities differ, giving what the authorities declare with their differences, and adding the author's own view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize authorities with impartiality, but do not hesitate to offer a reasoned personal judgment agreeable to reason and common sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical systems should be cheap, simple, effective, and adaptable
rubrics_metrics.description: Gouge's system of ventilation has given general satisfaction as a cheap, simple, and effective method; it is adapted for many kinds of buildings and can be applied with little alteration of plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design household/architectural systems for broad applicability and ease of retrofitting to existing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary textbooks should meet classroom needs and motivate further study
rubrics_metrics.description: Elements of Quaternions: exhibit elementary principles and notation of quaternion calculus so as to meet the wants of beginners in the class-room and to give them a conception of value and beauty leading to extended application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear elementary exposition, notation, and motivating examples that enable classroom adoption and encourage study of primary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical/clinical treatises should present careful analysis with typical case accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the Opium-Habit treatise is to place in the hands of the profession a carefully arranged analysis of the peculiar physical condition induced by the habit, with descriptions of the symptoms and the changes that take place under treatment, presented by accounts of typical cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include symptom descriptions, pathology, treatment approaches, and case histories; note organizational features (table of contents/index) — their absence is a shortcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Works must be grounded in careful investigation and study
rubrics_metrics.description: An active mind without the knowledge gained by investigation and careful study produces works mixing good ideas with utmost confusion of what history and science teach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unfounded assumptions and ensure arguments are supported by historical and scientific evidence; sound handling of topics like economics or cosmogony requires research-based grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include clear organization aids (table of contents, index)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opium-habit book 'has neither table of contents nor index.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-organized medical/scientific works should include a table of contents and an index to aid professional use and reference; their absence diminishes usability.
